name: Four cameras behind the nets (low and high at each end), two at the sides
notes: Cameras 7 (low) and 9 (high) are behind one net; 8 (low) and 10 (high) behind the other.
Cameras 5 and 6 are at the sides.
Low cameras sit close behind the net, so the goalie and net fill more of the view: a bigger
area is ignored. High cameras see over the net and down the ice, so they also give the long
view used when play is far from every camera (e.g. the neutral zone).
Cameras are re-aimed every game, so nothing here depends on exact positions.
No readable scoreboard is described: clocks are found automatically in each game.
Grid cells refer to a 16 x 9 grid over each camera's frame (row 0 = top).
